[M] Suggestion on how to organize.

There seem to be several ages, each can be cataloged independently, since revelation of the history happened that way. Here might be some loose "buckets" of how to collect and sort the historical events:

  1. In the Beginning: All was when creation occurred, and that which immediately followed. Things like light and dark, physics, elements, and principles (balance, entropy, etc)

  2. The Great Collection: All interactions between those first principles. The collection of elements into matter, planets, celestial bodies, and phenomenons (water/tides, fire, etc)

  3. Life, uhh, finds a way: Yuna creates life, and other Gods raise up beings and elementals to serve/honor themselves. (Death and Decay here, earlier or later, depending on how you feel)

  4. Love and Hate: As races sprout up, some Gods and their followers ally themselves with each other, and begin to oppose others. War and murder rise, as well as worship and benevolent blessings for good deeds.

  5. The First Reformation: Some call for chaos and disillusionment, some call for greater order. The Pantheon of Gods swells as life creates for itself new arenas, and the Gods seek to guide the living things of the world.

  6. The Forgotten: After the First Reformation, some Gods could see that all would eventually end, and be forgotten. Many Gods create their own realms as bastions to themselves, as workshops, and places of refuge and solitude.

  7. Partnership among Gods and Mortals: Lore and creations of great power have been spread throughout the world and the Realms of the Gods. Some Gods bestow blessings upon the creations of others, curse others, and take direct action towards other Gods. Lines have been drawn and rivalries emerge more solidly. The races of the world organize themselves and create structures by which they can live.

X. The End of Things: Entropy rules all. All will become dust, in time. With the creation of writing and the cycle of life and death so evident to all the races of the world, it may be well to ponder, "how does it all end?"

So the advantage of these buckets is that we don't have to tell the story literally in a chronological fashion because the section on life could be built out before the creation of the world. However, chronology gets a bit easier since it's not necessary to remember the post history when writing the life and times of savagegods.

Just some notions on a Sunday afternoon.
